Minsc of Rashemen is a recruitable Companion. He and  Jaheira return from both Baldur's Gate and Baldur's Gate II: Shadows of Amn and are the only two recruitable companions who cannot be romanced.[1] He is a Human and a Hunter Ranger with the Folk Hero background.

Minsc can first be found in The Counting House, where he has been tadpole-converted by the Absolute into a True Soul and criminal gang-leader known as the Stone Lord. He can be found again in the Abandoned Cistern; knocking him out in the ensuing fight allows him to be freed from his brainwashing.

After spending nearly a century  Petrified together, Minsc and his beloved hamster sidekick  Boo have finally been revived, and they seek a life of "butt-kicking" evil-doers to serve as a force of goodness, justice, and glory.

Minsc is also the only character with access to the spell  Find Familiar: Boo.

Though voiced by Matthew Mercer, Minsc was motion-captured by other actors, Neil Newbon amongst them.

“
If there is one thing Minsc hates more than beasts with bad breath - It is those who are tricksome with the truth! And turnips. But you are no turnip. Let that be of comfort, in your final moments.
„
— Minsc, threatening Rakath Glitterbeard

Overview

Starting class

When first encountered, Minsc is a level 12 Ranger with the following Ability Scores: 20 STR, 15 DEX, 15 CON, 6 INT, 8 WIS, 9 CHA. If recruited he reverts to a level 1 Ranger with the standard ability scores for that Class. His default subclass is Hunter. Minsc has the Folk Hero background.

Personal quest

Minsc does not have a personal quest, but he is directly tied to two others. First, he is the unwilling antagonist of Jaheira's companion quest ⁠The High Harper, and completing this quest allows him to join the party. Second, his ending in the Epilogue is determined by the outcome of ⁠Aid the Underduke, namely a conversation with  Nine-Fingers Keene afterward.

Recruitment

Minsc can be recruited during Act Three if Jaheira joined the party in Act Two. Progressing The High Harper leads to a fight with Minsc in the Lower City Sewers. To be recruited, he must be  knocked-out on the final blow, otherwise Minsc  dies without the possibility of being revived and Jaheira permanently leaves the party.

 The Emperor argues the Rashemi is too stupid to be of use but can be persuaded to extend the mind shield of the  Mysterious Artefact in order to free Minsc from the Absolute's influence:

  • [HISTORY] His chaos saved the city before. We need him. (DC 15)
  • [INTIMIDATION] You will do as I command, or I will find a way without you. (DC 15)

If Jaheira is dead, has not been recruited, or has left the party, the Emperor mentions he is "too far gone" and Minsc becomes hostile again with 1 hit point. After killing Minsc in this way, when spoken to, party members behave as though Jaheira had just left, even if she has never been with the party since Moonrise Towers.

Approaching Minsc with the player character elsewhere and only Jaheira in the party may cause odd behaviour, possibly preventing him from being recruited.

Leaving the party

Minsc's recruitment is tied to  Jaheira and anything that causes her to leave will take Minsc along with her. This includes sacrificing her to  Sarevok, killing her children or accepting  Bhaal's blessing as the  Dark Urge (or intimidating her to leave if they obtained the Slayer Form beforehand).

Approval

Main article: Minsc/Approval

Minsc is not the brightest, but he is brave and loyal - and has the cutest familiar:  Boo.[2]

Romance

Minsc cannot be romanced, remaining oblivious to any player character's possible attraction.

Description

Appearance

Minsc is a towering, muscle-bound man; his clean-shaven scalp bears a vivid purple crescent that sweeps over his right brow and cheek, and his steel-gray eyes rest beneath heavy brows. Old nicks crisscross his broad arms like a map of hard-won battles. Plain silver-looped earrings, weather-stained studded leather beneath a scarlet sash, and a well-worn longsword slung across his back all underscore his  Rashemi origins. Perched on his left shoulder sits a tiny brown hamster, whiskers twitching, the only soft edge to his otherwise imposing frame.

Personality

Minsc is a skilled warrior who is otherwise blissfully bereft of the burdens of Intellect. He believes his friend Boo is actually a  miniature giant space hamster and that he is the only one who can talk to him. He views the world in absolutes (no pun intended): if there is evil then it should be defeated.

Despite her constant nagging, Minsc sees Jaheira as a dear friend and is very protective of her, going so far as to call her his honorary  Wychlaran upon their reunion in Act Three. He intensely dislikes  Viconia DeVir and  Sarevok Anchev because of his history with the latter and because they are evil.

Backstory

See  Minsc for a more complete backstory

Minsc is a Rashemaar berserker from a matriarchal nation of Rashemen. As a young man, he went on a dajemma - a coming-of-age tradition for Rashemi men to travel the world accompanying his Wychlaran - a young witch  Dynaheir.

The Iron Crisis

In their travels, they became separated and Dynaheir was snatched by gnolls. With the help of  Gorion's Ward (the protagonist of the previous Baldur's Gate games) Minsc freed her and they travelled together, along with  Imoen, Jaheira and Khalid.

They resolved the  Iron Crisis and defeated the culprit -  Sarevok Anchev.

Shadows of Amn

Sometime after Sarevok's defeat, the group parted ways for a while until they once again joined up alongside their friends: Gorion's Ward, Imoen, Jaheira and Khalid. At some point in their travels, they were captured in a forest by  Shadow Thieves and imprisoned in a dungeon beneath the city of  Athkatla in Amn. Minsc, Jaheira and Imoen survived, but Dynaheir and Khalid were killed. Their captor was  Jon Irenicus - an elven wizard who wanted to steal the Bhaalspawn essence for himself. Minsc eventually helped Gorion's Ward to defeat him.

Petrified for a century

At some point in their travels, Minsc and Boo were ambushed by an unknown individual, petrified, and left in the middle of marketplace in the Upper City of Baldur's Gate. For a long time, Baldurians (including Jaheira) believed it was a statue, commissioned by a merchant to commemorate the city's renowned heroes. It became a popular landmark under the title "Beloved Ranger".

80 years later, a wild mage named  Delina tried to defend herself against a gargoyle and accidentally struck the statue with a  wild magic surge. The surge dispelled the petrification, and Minsc and Boo returned to life, unaware of the passing of time. They joined forces and travelled together for a time.

Approximately 10 years later, Minsc reunited with Jaheira. Together, they worked to uncover the mysterious Cult of the Absolute and were the first to reveal information about this threat. Unfortunately, Minsc's impulsive eagerness to fight resulted in his capture by the cultists and Jaheira, realising that they were severely unprepared and unarmed against this cult, decided to leave him in order to share news about this growing threat.

Captured by the cult, Minsc was infected with a Tadpole and brainwashed into following a  Doppelganger imitating  Jaheira. Under the tadpole's influence, he became a feared murderer under the moniker "Stone Lord". Minsc was also separated from Boo as the tadpole suppressed his memory of the hamster. Their latest crime is robbing the Counting House.

Involvement

Act Three

During Act Three, should the party arrive at the Counting House and delve into the vaults, they encounter Minsc accompanied by a doppelganger imitating Jaheira, with Minsc revealing himself by tearing his way out of the maw of a Mimic. When encountering Minsc in the Counting House he immediately leaves the building.

Epilogue

Minsc's appearance and dialogue at the party depend on the outcome of ⁠Aid the Underduke and the subsequent conversation with  Nine-Fingers Keene.

Ambient chatter from Minsc in either ending has him impressed with the quality of meat Withers provides, though neither he nor  Boo knows where Withers sourced it.

Zhentarim Prisoner

If Minsc is not present for the conversation with Nine-Fingers, he refuses to make amends with her or the player character sides with the Zhentarim, he arrives looking worse for wear, decked in rags. Without knowing the gravity of his situation, he reveals he has been kidnapped by the Zhentarim and was nearly about to be executed until Withers rescued him by spiriting him away for the party.

Berserker Lodge

If Minsc agrees to help the Guild as their "berserker lodge", he appears well-dressed and accompanied by a halfling from the Guild,  Happy Hoarson, whom he was in the middle of terrorizing for looting corpses. Minsc commends the player character and their companions for being ideal heroic role models, the kind of people Happy should strive to be more like. He also says that he no longer sleeps in "that" sewer; instead he has found a much nicer sewer to sleep in.

An additional line of ambient chatter from Minsc in this ending has him exclaiming to Boo that Happy must be treated nicely if he is to reform.

Speak with Dead

Minsc can be spoken to with  Speak with Dead, although several dialogue options only show up based on if the player knows that information already. Mentioning Boo turns his focus towards it and nothing else


If Minsc was not saved from the Absolute:

  • What is your real name, Stone Lord?
    • Minsc
      Minsc... of... Rashemen...
  • What did you want in the Counting House?
    • Minsc
      Zhentarim... precious... treasure...
      • Did you have anything of value worth taking?
        • Minsc
          ...Boo... BOO... BOO!...
      • You were paying the Zhentarim? What for?
        • Minsc
          ...Boo! BOO!... (If Boo mentioned)
        • Minsc
          Kill... Nine-Fingers... seize... Guildhall...

If Minsc witnessed the Dark Urge accept Bhaal:

  • Why did you make me kill you?
    • Minsc
      ...Boo... (If Boo mentioned)
    • Minsc
      Believed... in you... wrong...
  • How did your Harpers know to wait in ambush?
    • Minsc
      ...Boo...?... (If Boo mentioned)
    • Minsc
      Jaheira... smarter than you... smarter... than Minsc...

If Minsc was reunited with Boo:

  • What will happen to Boo without you?
    • Minsc
      ...Boo... BOO... BOO!...

Development

Unlike other companions, Minsc, alongside  Jaheira, was revealed in a trailer at the Video Game Awards 2022. Minsc was initially slated to be a playable origin, his scrapped content was datamined back in 2020. Tieflings in the Emerald Grove had special dialogue reactions to him and his hamster.

Changes from previous games

Unlike Jaheira, whose stats remained fairly consistent through the games, Minsc's Ability Scores in Baldur's Gate 3 differ heavily from his stats from  Baldur's Gate 1 & 2. In previous games, he is depicted as immensely strong, being able to punch through walls and break himself out of cages. However, his stats as a companion in Baldur's Gate 3 do not reflect this. This is likely due to the fact that while previous games use stat rolling, Baldur's Gate 3 uses 27 Point-Buy; it also allows his Ranger abilities to function more reliably due to his high Wisdom.

If one seeks to emulate Minsc's ability scores from prior incarnations of the game, an arguably close approximation is: STR 17, DEX 15, CON 15, INT 8, WIS 8, CHA 10. This distribution leaves only STR and WIS as unattainable outliers at the start of the game, as his previous STR is 18, (requiring an ASI) and his WIS 6 - which would be problematic for a Ranger in Fifth Edition.

The NPC Version of Minsc encountered in the Sewers uses a stat-block reminiscent of the previous entries in the series: STR 20, DEX 15, CON 15, INT 8, WIS 6, CHA 9. He swaps to his playable version after the conversation introducing Boo to the party.

In Baldur's Gate 3, Minsc is voiced by Matthew Mercer, replacing Jim Cummings from previous games.
